source_text: Non est enim qui subveniat reis, quando ipse, qui est unus, desiderio creandarum miseriarum etiam eos punit, in quibus nihil aliud quam hoc, quod ipse fecit, agnoscit.
pass_a_gloss: For there is not who may come under to the guilty, when he himself, who is one, by a desire of creating miseries even punishes those, in whom he recognizes nothing other than this, which he himself made.
pass_b_english: For no one remains to help the guilty when the one who alone is God, from a desire to create misery, punishes even those in whom he recognizes nothing except what he himself made.

choices.why: Loaded word in Julian's Latin at 1.121; English follows LS/Blaise range without copying NPNF.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
